assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pores, framework topology and active sites (organic structure-directing agents, new frameworks, shape-selective acid and metal catalysis) is a clear case of architecture determining function, and it underpins refining, petrochemicals, emissions control and fine-chemicals production at industrial scale. Impact is large, lasting and visible well beyond academia.
assessment.attribution: Corma (zeolite catalysis design and diversity of catalytic applications), Davis (framework synthesis and structure-directing concepts) and Zones (organic-template synthesis of commercially central frameworks such as SSZ-type materials) are the strongest three-person configuration. Yu, Tsapatsis and others made important but more specialised contributions, and zeolite chemistry also has earlier foundational figures not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent confirmation, commercial deployment and crystallographic characterisation, so timing is not premature. I note that this is my own field, which is a reason to test my enthusiasm against the committee's wider view.
uncertainties: The prize must be framed as design principles rather than a catalogue of materials, and the discovery is diffuse across many groups.
Allocation among synthesis, structure-direction and catalysis contributions is unresolved and risks omitting early pioneers outside the supplied credit.
Part of my familiarity comes from the same community, so I may over-weight it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers lets structures be determined from micro- and nanocrystals before radiation damage ('diffraction before destruction') and enables time-resolved molecular movies. It opened structure determination for samples that conventional crystallography cannot handle, which parallels the enabling-method logic I value strongly.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu contributed the conceptual basis of diffraction before destruction, Chapman led the first proof-of-principle SFX experiments and the data-analysis framework, and Fromme worked on membrane-protein nanocrystals central to the demonstration. Schlichting and others are also major contributors and others outside the list (for example on injectors and data processing) were essential, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Maturing: results are independently reproduced at several facilities and time-resolved studies are producing mechanistic insight, though impact on routine structural chemistry is still limited by beamtime access.
uncertainties: Beamtime scarcity limits breadth of impact compared with synchrotron methods.
Crowded attribution including injector, sample-delivery and software developers not on the list.
Whether the most important results are methodological or the mechanistic findings it has enabled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The identification and structural characterisation of multiwalled carbon nanotubes by high-resolution electron microscopy opened a new class of one-dimensional carbon materials, with major impact on nanoscience, composites and electronics. The structural evidence rests directly on TEM imaging and diffraction, which I find convincing and appropriate for the field.
assessment.attribution: Iijima's 1991 observation and subsequent single-wall nanotube work (the latter reported independently with Ichihashi and by Bethune and colleagues) are the best-documented decisive contribution; the supplied names include Bethune and Endo, whose priority claims for single-wall tubes and earlier filament observations are real but less clear. A single-laureate award around Iijima is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: more than three decades of confirmation and development, though applications have been slower than early expectations.
uncertainties: Prior observations of hollow carbon filaments (Endo and others) complicate priority.
The discovery is arguably as much physics and materials science as chemistry.
Practical impact has lagged the scientific impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another without double-strand cleavage, using a chemically conceived fusion of a deaminase with a programmable DNA-binding protein. It is a precise, general enabling tool already in clinical use and widely adopted, and it follows directly from a chemical-biology design logic.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the design and the proof of principle, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors of the original studies. Kondo and Nishida independently reported a related cytidine-deaminase approach, which complicates but does not remove a Liu-centred award; a single laureate seems defensible and the CRISPR-Cas9 prize already recognised the underlying nuclease.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: rapid independent adoption, multiple clinical trials, and demonstrated therapeutic effects, though long-term safety outcomes are still being established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 genome-editing prize could make the committee reluctant.
Credit with Komor and Gaudelli (trainees) and the independent Kondo and Nishida work.
Long-term clinical safety and off-target effects are not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines accessible under general, mild conditions with tunable ligands and is used routinely in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. The methodology is broad, clear in concept and heavily used.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, ligand-controlled catalytic amination independently and in parallel, giving a natural two-person configuration. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor rather than the general method.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with extensive independent use; the main question is timing relative to the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize.
uncertainties: The committee may regard it as an extension of the 2010 prize.
Whether Hartwig's and Buchwald's contributions are considered distinct enough from earlier precursors.
This is outside my own expertise, so my assessment of the synthetic literature is less secure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into inducers of proteasomal degradation of chosen proteins (PROTACs and molecular glues), opening a new pharmacological modality including for formerly undruggable targets. The conceptual advance and the design of heterobifunctional molecules are strongly chemical.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept, Ciulli contributed structure-guided design and VHL ligands, whereas the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito and others) links to thalidomide mechanism; these strands may need different recognition and the supplied credit does not cleanly settle it.
assessment.maturity: Somewhat early: many candidates are in clinical trials, but approved drugs and long-term validation are still limited.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete.
PROTAC and molecular-glue strands may require different attribution.
Structural evidence for ternary complexes varies across systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The crystal structures of nitrogenase, including the FeMo cofactor with its interstitial carbide and later turnover-related states, provide an atomic-level framework for biological nitrogen fixation, an essential chemical transformation. This is structural evidence at its best and has driven bioinorganic and catalyst-design work.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the first nitrogenase structures and cofactor architecture; Einsle resolved the central light atom in the cluster at higher resolution. Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe contributed biochemistry, genetics and cluster biosynthesis, which are significant but different in kind.
assessment.maturity: Substantial but incomplete: structure is well established, while the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding site remain debated.
uncertainties: The reaction mechanism is not settled.
Whether a structural prize without mechanistic closure is timely.
The biochemistry and biosynthesis contributions could be left out in a small laureate group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts define a limit of atom-efficient heterogeneous catalysis, with isolated metal sites on oxide supports shown by aberration-corrected electron microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy. The concept has produced a large, active field with possible links between homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Fe/FeOx and Pt1/FeOx work of Zhang, Qiao, Wang, Liu and Li coined the term and supplied the first well-characterised examples, with theory from Li. Earlier isolated-site chemistry (for example on zeolites and oxides) weakens a claim of a single decisive origin.
assessment.maturity: Premature to mid-maturity: reproducibility and the true nature of active sites under reaction conditions are still debated, and industrial impact is limited.
uncertainties: Active-site identity and stability under working conditions are contested.
Priority relative to earlier isolated-site catalysts.
Limited commercial application so far.
